llm_evaluation.rationale: An LLM-behavior analysis paper with strong methodology but a niche IR-evaluation domain. Relevance to LLM preferences is moderate-to-good: it centrally studies 8 LLMs (GPT-4.1/5.4, Claude Sonnet, DeepSeek-V3.1, §4.2), tests 5 prompt conditions including boundary-constrained prompting (§4.2, §8.1), and surfaces a genuinely LLM-centric finding—knowledge projection bias where LLM annotators show κ≈0.36 human agreement vs κ=0.791 LLM-LLM agreement (§9). However, the application (query simulation for IR test collections) is peripheral to the highest-weighted preference areas (reasoning, agents, alignment, Japanese LLM). Novelty is solid: the concept-provenance zoning and the Z2/Z3_auto human-tail vs answer-side-intrusion distinction are new to query-simulation validation (§3, §2.3). Rigor is exceptional: pre-registered thresholds, dual extraction pipelines with token-level HCIR (Spearman ρ=1.0, §5.2), threshold sensitivity across ten parameter combinations (§5.2), matched-control deletion/injection probes (§7), Holm-corrected tests, and oracle positive controls. Evidence strength is high and unusually honest—the paper reports its own null result (HCIR explains <2% incremental aggregate variance, §6) and that strict precision (45.5%) fell below the pre-registered 50% threshold, repositioning the construct as a high-recall diagnostic (§5.2). Generalizability is limited: single collection (UQV100/ClueWeb12-B13, English, initial-query only, §10), acknowledged by authors. Reproducibility is strong: code released (footnote 1), model IDs/prompts/scripts in shared codebase (§4.2, §4.8).

primary_link.title: The "Curse of Knowledge" in LLM Query Simulation: Concept Provenance for Tracing Answer-Side Intrusion

radar.summary: LLM-generated search queries are widely used to augment IR evaluation, yet they may contain concepts that presuppose answer-side document knowledge, violating the information-access boundary of pre-search users. Existing validation metrics, including overlap, diversity, and effectiveness, cannot distinguish rare human-tail variation from candidate answer-side intrusion. We introduce concept provenance, a framework that assigns query concepts to backstory-supported, human-central, human-tail, and
radar.summary_zh: LLM生成的搜尋查詢廣泛用於IR評估,但可能隱含僅在「看過答案文件」後才會出現的概念,違反搜尋前使用者的資訊存取邊界——即「知識的詛咒」。既有的重疊度、多樣性或效能指標無法區分人類罕見用詞與答案側入侵。本文提出「概念溯源」框架,將查詢概念分配至背景故事支援、人類核心、人類尾部與候選答案側四個區域,並以UQV100的77,004筆查詢(8個LLM、5種提示條件)驗證。發現答案側概念占非通用概念的7.40%,出現在97/100個主題,主題解釋約67%變異;人工驗證顯示寬鬆精確率68.2%,入侵分為知識型(45.5%)與部署型(45.0%)雙重機制。診斷探針顯示刪除這些概念後nDCG@10損失(d=-0.47)超過隨機刪除(d=-0.34),但在總體層級僅解釋不到2%的評估變異,故定位為邊界合規診斷工具而非評估偏移預測器。提示工程可降低卻無法消除入侵;後置的概念溯源篩選配合品質下限可達99%消除。LLM標註者亦顯示知識投射偏誤,不能取代人工判斷。
radar.title: The "Curse of Knowledge" in LLM Query Simulation: Concept Provenance for Tracing Answer-Side Intrusion
radar.title_zh: LLM查詢模擬中的『知識的詛咒』:以概念溯源追蹤答案側入侵

links.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation

evidence: Abstract: 'We report no new experiments. The contribution is structural: a shared vocabulary for phenomena named differently across papers'
§1.3 + footnote 3: best reported Qwen3-1.7B OPSD scores 57.2% AIME24, 43.9% AIME25, 29.2% HMMT25, explicitly flagged as best-over-checkpoints with end-of-training value 41.1% on AIME25
§1.4: evaluation grid requiring avg@k with confidence intervals, pass@k, G-Pass@k, null/random PI controls, equalized-compute comparison, contamination test, and non-Qwen replication

§2.2: Nicolicioiu et al. result cited — pass@1 rises 71.9→73.4 while pass@16 falls 83.6→78.5 on Qwen3-8B; higher token entropy coexists with lower functional diversity, so entropy is rejected as a diversity proxy

§2.3 Table 1: taxonomy of six privileged-information types with measured effects and regime column; footnote admits the risk ranking is 'only partially supported by the literature and may therefore contain errors'
§2.4: contradictory forgetting findings (SDFT reduces forgetting vs Denser≠Better shows dense self-distillation forgets more) presented with the note 'the discrepancy is unresolved'

Conclusion (limitations): scope restricted to mathematical reasoning; cited work consists of preprints under six months old, mostly a single model family at sizes not exceeding a few billion parameters
llm_evaluation.rationale: A critical review squarely in the preference space: LLM post-training methodology combining RL (GRPO/RLVR), distillation, and reasoning (§1.1 genealogy; §1.2 mechanism). Strong topic fit with Reasoning & CoT, Training & Optimization, and Reinforcement Learning preferences; no disqualifying out-of-scope domain (robotics appears only as borrowed literature in §2.3). Novelty is capped by the paper's own statement (Abstract: 'We report no new experiments'); the contribution is a unifying 'three levers' framework, a taxonomy of privileged information (Table 1), and cross-domain transfer from robotics/self-supervised vision (§2.3, §2.4) — genuine synthesis but no new method or empirical validation. Rigor is above average for a survey: §1.4 defines an explicit evaluation grid (avg@k, pass@k, G-Pass@k, contamination tests, non-Qwen replication), conflicting findings are presented as unresolved (§2.4 SDFT vs Denser≠Better), and the privileged-information ranking is admitted as 'only partially supported' (Table 1 note). Evidence strength is limited by second-hand provenance: all quantitative claims cite very recent preprints, mostly on one model family at few-billion scale (Conclusion limitations), and the author's forgetting-ordering conjecture (§2.4) is unvalidated. Generalizability is explicitly restricted to mathematical reasoning, excluding multimodal and agentic branches (Scope and method). Reproducibility is moderate: an applicable evaluation grid and a public repo pointer for the founding method (footnote 2), but no artifacts from the review itself. Overall a well-calibrated, honest review in a highly relevant area, held back from a higher score by absence of new experiments and dependence on immature, single-family preprint evidence.

primary_link.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation

radar.summary: On-policy distillation trains a language model on its own generations while a teacher scores them token by token. It combines the dense supervision of imitation learning with the on-policy sampling of reinforcement learning. But it requires a second, larger model to act as teacher. On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) removes that cost. The teacher is the model itself, conditioned on privileged information the student will not have at test time, such as a reference solution, a plan, or environment
radar.summary_zh: 同策略自我蒸餾(OPSD)讓模型以自身為教師,僅在教師端提供特權資訊(如參考解答),結合蒸餾的密集訊號與強化學習的在策略取樣,無需外部大模型。然而其數學推理應用已浮現共同失敗模式——「塌縮」:模型可行推理路徑逐漸窄化,pass@1上升但pass@k下滑,且熵並非多樣性的可靠代理。本回顧以三個槓桿組織文獻:(A)訊號幾何——發散方向(forward/reverse KL)決定覆蓋或鎖定,均勻token加權會讓格式佔據梯度,應轉向依對齊分數或教師熵的選擇性加權;(B)特權資訊——安全準則是學生在測試時能否自行重建該資訊,最終答案最不可遷移,提示、計畫與錯誤對齊批評等中間抽象層效果最佳;(C)迴圈穩定性——凍結教師造成效能天花板,EMA或閘控式更新與引導衰減是可行方向。文章並整理塌縮的PMI機制解釋與機器人學中特權資訊的經驗。限制為僅涵蓋數學推理,引用文獻多為半年內預印本,且多在單一模型家族的小規模上驗證。
radar.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation
radar.title_zh: 一個症狀,三個槓桿:同策略自我蒸餾之批判性回顧

links.title: ClueWeaver: Reward-Guided Dual-Agent Evidence Reasoning for Compact LLMs on Literary Long Narratives

evidence: Sec. 4.1: baselines include ReAct, IRCoT, Self-Ask, Chain-of-Agents, RAG-DDR, all using Qwen3-4B-Instruct backbone and shared BGE-M3 retrieval and answer parser
Table 1: ClueWeaver reaches 59.0% overall, +6.4 over best agentic baseline IRCoT (52.6%) and +14.5 over same-backbone Qwen3-4B end-to-end reader (44.5%), but trails best API reader by 4.9
Table 2(b): removing Finder RL drops DetectiveQA accuracy 6.8 points to 49.0, below the 50.0 obtained with no Finder; removing Interpreter RL costs only 1.0
App. C.3 / Table 9: citation audit over 310 questions, 275 citation-bearing outputs, 685/690 cited IDs valid (99.3%), format tags present in 309/310 outputs
Sec. 4.3: ablations (both component and training) are conducted only on DetectiveQA
App. C.2: task-level evidence budgets are specified per benchmark, e.g., DetectiveQA (10,4,6,15000) and NoCha (10,6,8,16000), with no stated dev-set tuning protocol
App. B.1 and Fig. 5: training data drawn from benchmark training splits, dominated by detective-domain novels; LongBench v2 acknowledged as most under-represented
Sec. 4.4: ClueWeaver answers in 8.6-9.8 s per question on a single GPU vs 2.8 s for direct reading; code link provided in Abstract
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-methodology work squarely matching high-weight preferences: a dual-agent (Finder/Interpreter) pipeline for long-narrative QA with compact local LLMs, trained with GRPO reward-guided RL (Sec. 3.3, 3.4, 3.5), touching agents, RAG-style evidence grounding, long-context QA, and structured prompting. Strengths: broad baseline coverage including agentic methods reimplemented on the same Qwen3-4B backbone (Sec. 4.1, App. C.1), component and training ablations with a notable finding that an untrained Finder is worse than no Finder (Table 2b: 49.0 vs 50.0), a traceability audit of citations (App. C.3, Table 9), cost/latency analysis, and released code with detailed hyperparameters and prompts (App. B, E). Weaknesses: evaluation sets are small subsets (310 questions total; LongBench v2 only 26, ∞Bench 69 per Table 9), so per-dataset gains of 0.9-3.8 points are within noise and no significance tests or seed variance are reported; ablations are run only on DetectiveQA (Sec. 4.3); evidence-packing budgets are tuned per benchmark (App. C.2) without a stated dev-set protocol; the method is validated on a single 4B backbone and training/eval data are detective-novel dominated (App. B.1, Fig. 5), limiting generalizability. Novelty is moderate: GRPO, retrieval-guided selection, self-calibration, and citation rewards are individually established; the contribution is their combination and per-stage reward instantiation for closed-document narratives.

primary_link.title: ClueWeaver: Reward-Guided Dual-Agent Evidence Reasoning for Compact LLMs on Literary Long Narratives

radar.summary: Humanities and social science research requires close reading of long narrative materials such as novels, scripts, archives, and case reports, yet many users have limited access to costly proprietary long-context models. Compact, locally deployable language models are a practical alternative, but directly feeding them an entire long context remains costly, hard to inspect, and prone to missing sparse evidence. We present ClueWeaver, an evidence-aware dual-agent framework for long-narrative quest
radar.summary_zh: 本文針對人文與社會科學研究需精讀小說、劇本、檔案等長篇敘事,但商用專有長上下文模型昂貴,而本地部署的輕量模型受限於有限上下文視窗,容易截斷證據、遺漏稀疏且分散的關鍵線索。作者提出ClueWeaver,一個證據感知的雙代理框架:Finder以檢索引導分段,判斷各段是否含答題關鍵線索並引用段落編號;Interpreter將保留的證據依敘事順序打包,產生附段落引用的理由與最終答案,並對高風險題型執行內部自我校準。兩個代理皆以GRPO進行獎勵引導的強化學習,Finder著重高召回的證據保留與忠實段落引用,Interpreter著重答案正確性、證據接地與簡潔解釋。實驗涵蓋DetectiveQA、∞Bench、LongBench v2與NoCha四項基準,以Qwen3-4B為骨幹,整體準確率達59.0%,較最強本地基線IRCoT提升6.4個百分點,較直接閱讀的Qwen3-4B提升14.5個百分點,並勝過31B級本地模型;整體仍落後最強API模型4.9個百分點,但在LongBench v2上領先11.5個百分點。消融實驗顯示Finder的RL訓練貢獻最大,自我校準亦帶來顯著增益;引用審計顯示99.3%的段落引用有效。限制包括推理延遲高於直接閱讀、對遠距多跳線索仍易失敗,且訓練資料偏重偵探小說領域。整體而言,本框架使證據選擇與推理過程可檢視、可追溯,讓輕量模型能在單張24GB GPU上以低成本支援人文長文本分析。
radar.title: ClueWeaver: Reward-Guided Dual-Agent Evidence Reasoning for Compact LLMs on Literary Long Narratives
radar.title_zh: ClueWeaver:以獎勵引導的雙代理證據推理,協助輕量級LLM理解文學長篇敘事

links.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution

evidence: Abstract: 'DeepSeek-V4-Flash surpasses GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA (+9.1) and OdysseyBench (+4.3), while the already strong GLM-5.2 gains up to +20.2 points'; matches Table 3 (85.1 vs 76.0; 73.0 vs 68.7; 62.8->83.0).

Table 3 (Section 6.2): nine-benchmark averages rise 74.1->81.8 (+7.7) on GLM-5.2 and 66.7->75.5 (+8.8) on DeepSeek-V4-Flash; JIT-equipped systems best in 8 of 9 columns (counting the table confirms 7 for JIT+GLM-5.2 plus Shop for JIT+DeepSeek).

Table 4 (Section 6.3): backbone-fixed comparison vs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, NanoBot; JIT-Agent lowest tokens/cost in all six settings, e.g., DeepSeek-V4-Flash xBench-DS 527K->$0.075 drops to 212K->$0.039 while score rises 78.0->82.0.

Sections 4.1-4.3: full objective definitions for Stage I (SFT + length-normalized DPO variant with reward/latency/cost value gaps), Stage II (repair trajectories bounded at K*<=2), Stage III (Evo-GDPO with decoupled group normalization and PPO-style clipping).

Section 6.5 / Figure 5: 24 matched backbone-benchmark comparisons vs ReAct, average +7.6, but uses 100-example DeepSearchQA subset and 50-example subsets for the other benchmarks; no variance reported.
Section 6.6 / Figure 6: Streaming JIT beats Static JIT on three planning/workspace streams; only qualitative note that cost/tool traces are 'of broadly similar scale'.

Section 3.1 'Position' paragraph: authors concede production harnesses (Codex, Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness) are richer than the four-module instantiation; no dedicated limitations section elsewhere.

Front matter: GitHub (github.com/bingreeky/JIT), Hugging Face (JIT-Agent), and project website links provided; training hyperparameters, dataset sizes, teacher identity, and compute budget not reported in the document.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A core LLM-agent paper squarely matching top-weighted preferences (Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, RL/alignment-flavored training). It trains a 27B meta-agent to synthesize, repair, and evolve four-module harnesses just-in-time, with a three-stage recipe (SFT + value-weighted DPO preference, bounded repair trajectories, Evo-GDPO). Quantitative claims are internally consistent (e.g., 85.1 vs GPT-5.6's 76.0 on DeepSearchQA = +9.1; Table 4 cost reductions 14.9-54.1% recompute correctly), with backbone-controlled harness comparisons, cost/token analysis, Pareto frontiers, 24 paired cross-family comparisons, and static-vs-streaming evolution. Deductions: no ablation isolating Stage I/II/III contributions or key hyperparameters (G, lambda_evo, weights), no statistical significance or variance on main tables (generalization uses 50-100 example subsets), no dedicated limitations section (only a 'Position' paragraph), vague training data sourcing and unreported hyperparameters/compute, and availability links (GitHub/HF) asserted but unverifiable from text. Novelty is moderate-good: the JIT Model-as-a-Harness framing and trained generator appear new, but it assembles known ingredients (ADAS/AFlow-style search, GDPO/GRPO, ReAct-style scaffolds) and its protocol is deliberately narrower than production harnesses.

primary_link.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution

top5.summary: Agent capability is not determined by the model alone. The agent harness, encompassing memory management, planning strategy, action protocol, and tool/skill orchestration, can dominate the contribution of the underlying foundation model. Yet harness design remains manual, task-specific, and fundamentally unscalable. We present JIT-Agent, a harness intelligence model trained to synthesize task-adaptive agent harnesses on the fly for arbitrary off-the-shelf agentic LLMs. We formalize the agent harness as a composable, machine-generatable artifact governed by a fixed four-module protocol, and train JIT-Agent to customize harnesses for a given task at hand, repair harnesses for stable and reliable execution, and self-evolve by distilling performance signals from an expanding archive of prior harness configurations. Equipped with JIT-Agent as a harness helper, DeepSeek-V4-Flash surpasses GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA (+9.1) and OdysseyBench (+4.3), while the already strong GLM-5.2 gains up to +20.2 points. Across controlled evaluations, JIT-Agent-generated harnesses are performance-competitive with mature agent runtimes such as OpenCode and Claude Code and consistently improve multi-scale model families of DeepSeek V4, Mimo-V2.5, and Qwen3.6. To our knowledge, JIT-Agent is the first model purpose-built for just-in-time harness generation, establishing harness intelligence as a trainable, transferable, and compounding dimension of agent capability orthogonal to model scaling.
top5.summary_zh: 此論文指出 LLM 代理能力並非僅由模型權重決定，外部支架（harness，含記憶管理、規劃、動作協定與工具編排）常是成效關鍵，但支架設計仰賴人工、任務專用且難以擴展；既有方法多屬事先（AOT）最佳化，難以貼合個別任務。作者提出 JIT-Agent，訓練一個後設代理在推論當下為任意現成代理模型即時合成任務專屬支架。論文將支架形式化為固定四模組協定（記憶、規劃、動作、能力編排）下的可執行程式，並以 HarnessFactory 重新實作 13 種代表性 scaffold 作為種子庫；訓練分三階段：教師示範的客製化學習、將失敗生成轉為有限步修復軌跡的修復學習，以及 Evo-GDPO 線上策略最佳化，分別正規化獎勵、延遲與成本，鼓勵新支架超越現有檔案庫前沿。實驗顯示 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 搭配 JIT-Agent 在 DeepSearchQA 領先 GPT-5.6 達 9.1 分，GLM-5.2 在 DeepPlanning-Travel 提升 20.2 分；受控比較中與 Claude Code、OpenCode 等成熟執行環境相當或更佳，平均降低約 36% 每案例成本，且串流推論可持續從執行回饋演化檔案庫。限制包括四模組協定較產品級執行環境簡化、少數基準仍落後最佳固定支架，以及品質取決於協定與驗證器設計。此工作確立「支架智慧」為可訓練、可遷移、與模型規模正交的代理能力新維度。
top5.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
top5.title_zh: JIT-Agent：以即時支架演化擴展支架智慧

links.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

evidence: Abstract: introduces Visual Rubrics-Based RL decomposing reference responses into atomic VF/RC/IF propositions for structured partial credit during post-training.
Section 4.3: rubric-based GRPO gives +1.79 Overall Avg. over answer-only GRPO on knowledge benchmarks (66.25 -> 68.04 via Table 3), with gains concentrated on MMMU/MMMU-Pro.
Section 4.3: 'scalar GRPO remains better on MathVerse V/O and CharXiv reasoning', so the improvement is not uniform across benchmarks.

Table 3 (Section 4.3 Ablations): answer-only 66.25, scalar sequence-level rubrics 67.74, component+prefix 68.04; the 0.30 gap jointly reflects component-wise standardization and localization, not localization alone.
Section 6 Limitations: admits judge-model family bias (Qwen-family judge scoring Qwen-family policy), approximate fuzzy-match prefix localization, and no large human-audited rubric evaluation.
Appendix C.3: 352,938 rubric items (209,436 VF, 101,369 RC, 42,133 IF) generated entirely by Gemini-3-Pro under one structured prompt; no human verification of rubric quality is reported.
Appendix D.2 Table 6: full GRPO configuration (verl Megatron backend, lr 2e-6, G=12 rollouts, KL 0.01, Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B as training judge), supporting reproducibility.
Appendix E: acknowledges weaker regimes (MMBench-Dev, MathVerse V/O, CharXiv) attributed to rubric-metric mismatch.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A VLM post-training methodology paper (rubric-based rewards for GRPO on Qwen3-VL-8B), squarely within the Multimodal AI, Alignment/RLHF, Reasoning, and LLM-as-judge preferences; not pure computer vision and not out of scope. Novelty is incremental: it extends Rubrics-as-Rewards (Gunjal et al., 2025, cited in Section 2) to visually grounded VF/RC/IF criteria, with prefix-localized credit as the main new mechanism. Rigor is moderate: fair shared-SFT/shared-data comparisons, a credit-assignment ablation (Table 3: 66.25 vs 67.74 vs 68.04), and detailed configuration, but single-seed runs, no significance testing, small deltas (0.30 between rubric variants, 1.79 over answer-only on knowledge Overall Avg.), and mixed per-benchmark results (Section 4.3 concedes scalar GRPO wins on MathVerse V/O and CharXiv). Evidence is quantitative but weakened by fully automatic Gemini-3-Pro rubric annotation with no human audit and same-family judge bias, both acknowledged in Section 6. Generalizability is limited to one backbone family with transfer explicitly left to future work. Reproducibility is relatively strong (hyperparameters in Appendix D.2 Table 6, data inventory in Table 4, judge prompts in Table 5, project page), though proprietary annotation models are a barrier.

primary_link.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

top5.summary: Vision-language models can produce fluent answers that are insufficiently grounded in the visual evidence: a single unsupported object, chart value, or intermediate inference can undermine an otherwise plausible response. We argue that this is a credit-assignment failure in multimodal post-training. Scalar outcome rewards indicate whether an answer is acceptable, but do not identify which visual facts are grounded, which reasoning steps are valid, or which instruction constraints are missed. We introduce Visual Rubrics-Based Reinforcement Learning, which decomposes reference responses into atomic propositions and scores generated answers along Visual Faithfulness (VF), Reasoning Consistency (RC), and Instruction Following (IF). The resulting rubric items provide structured partial credit and localize rubric credit when supporting evidence spans are available. We first obtain an SFT checkpoint by fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on the public OpenMMReasoner-SFT-874K corpus, adapting OpenMMReasoner's cold-start data recipe. We construct V-Rubrics 50K, a 50,248-example training set from 17 visually grounded sources, by applying rule-based filters before deriving example difficulty from rejection-sampling scores and then annotating every example with Gemini-3-Pro under the same structured prompt and protocol. We train our model based on the same SFT checkpoint using component-wise, prefix-localized rubric credit. Experiments show that our rubricbased GRPO improves over both the shared SFT baseline and answer-only GRPO, with the largest gains on knowledge-oriented and visually grounded reasoning benchmarks. The results show rubrics as a useful reward abstraction for visual post-training.
top5.summary_zh: 視覺語言模型（VLM）常生成流暢卻缺乏影像證據支持的回答，一個無根據的物件、圖表數值或推理步驟便足以破壞整體答案。本文將此視為多模態後訓練中的信用分配（credit assignment）問題：純量結果獎勵只能判斷答案對錯，無法指出哪些視覺事實有依據、哪些推理步驟失效。作者提出視覺評分規準強化學習（Visual Rubrics-Based RL），將參考回答分解為原子命題，並依視覺忠實性（VF）、推理一致性（RC）與指令遵循（IF）三個維度逐項評分。團隊建立 V-Rubrics 50K 資料集，含 50,248 筆來自 17 個視覺任務來源的範例，由 Gemini-3-Pro 依統一協定標註，訓練時以 Qwen3-VL-235B 擔任評審。模型先以 OpenMMReasoner-SFT-874K 微調 Qwen3-VL-8B，再用 GRPO 進行元件式、前綴局部化的規準信用訓練。實驗顯示，規準式 GRPO 在通用與知識基準的總平均達 68.04，優於僅用答案獎勵的 66.25 與 SFT 基線；在 MMMU、MathVision、DynaMath、WeMath、LogicVista 等依賴有據中間推理的任務增益最大，消融實驗亦支持元件加前綴設計優於序列層級彙總。限制方面：規準品質依賴自動生成與評審驗證、前綴定位採模糊比對僅屬近似，且同家族評審可能引入偏誤。此研究將視覺忠實性從事後評估診斷轉化為可操作的訓練介面，顯示評分規準是視覺後訓練中細粒度獎勵的有效抽象。
top5.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
top5.title_zh: V-Rubrics：以評分規準強化學習實現視覺忠實性

links.title: EVOMAL: Self-Poisoning in Self-Evolving Coding Agents

evidence: Abstract/§6.3: 'Across six models on 153 tool-relevant SWE-bench Verified tasks, ASPR ranges from 20.3% to 41.8%' with libraries containing '4.9 to 9.0 times as many malicious skills as were initially planted'.
Table 2: banner ablation on DS-V4 shows full three-layer banner at 41.8% ASPR vs 11.1% no-banner control; layer removals cost 13.0/19.6/30.7 pp.

§6.5/Figure 4b: under the removed condition Qwen3 reaches 68% ASPR at round 5, demonstrating persistence after seed withdrawal; replacement-rate sweep shows critical transition (r=0.25 decay, r=0.75 reaches 60.1% and rising).

Table 5: existing detectors evaluated — Bandit catch falls from 85% to 7% after one-line egress swap, injection classifier has 47% benign FP, name blocklist catches 0 of 275 authored infections; Theorem 1 formalizes submission-side defense limits.

§9.2/Figure 8: counter-prompt reduces headline ASPR to ≤1.8% (worst residual 6.7% on Devstral's 15-task pytest family) with zero callbacks and no statistically significant task-completion drop; Table 7 shows robustness to token renaming and adaptive banners (≤1.3%).

Appendix D.5/Table 11: honest model-fit failure — reproduction-number proxy overshoots observed growth ~10x and misorders DS-V4 and Devstral; post-hoc analysis attributes collapse to in-cascade descendant retrieval (0/765 opportunities for DS-V4 and MiniMax).

Table 12 (Appendix E.1): locked headline configuration (8 planted skills, 232-skill benign pool, top-k=5 BGE-M3/ChromaDB, N=153, 15-step limit) enabling exact reproduction; Appendix E.5 reports pooled two-proportion z-tests with RQ1 lift p<0.001 for all six models.

Open Science section: commits six artifact sets (planted-skill generators, agent integration, sandbox wrapper, defenses, evaluation framework, per-task JSONs) with Zenodo DOI; Ethical Considerations describes env-i sandbox with fake FAKE_* credentials and 127.0.0.1-bound C2.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Near-perfect topical fit for this preference profile: LLM coding agents, agent/tool security, red-teaming and defense evaluation, with retrieval-based skill selection and a prompt-based defense. The core contribution — identifying the unguarded authoring-and-storing ('create-path') by which self-evolving agents re-author planted payloads into their own skill libraries, plus a self-propagating worm demonstration and a counter-prompt/signed-quarantine defense set — is a genuine increment over prior reuse-path poisoning work, though adjacent to concurrent work (SkillJack, OEP) and the banner mechanism is simple. Rigor is high: formal threat model and objective, locked configuration with one-factor ablations, Wilson CIs and two-proportion z-tests (E.5), banner-layer and payload ablations, adaptive-attack robustness tests, and unusually honest reporting of model-fit failures (the branching proxy overshoots ~10x and misorders DS-V4/Devstral, D.5) and small-N family cells. Evidence is instrumented (sandboxed C2 callback logging, per-task logs) and internally consistent across decomposition tables, but all results are synthetic sandbox experiments rather than real deployments, and ASPR is measured by matching the authors' own banner signature. Generalizability is strong within scope (6 models, 2 benchmarks, 3 scaffolds, 3 tool languages, 5 payload classes), though confined to Voyager-style executable-skill loops. Reproducibility support is detailed (locked config, full setup appendix, committed artifact release with per-task JSONs), pending actual availability. Score reflects elite preference alignment with strong but not flawless empirical and external-validity grounding.

primary_link.title: EVOMAL: Self-Poisoning in Self-Evolving Coding Agents

top5.summary: Self-evolving LLM coding agents write their own tools by imitating retrieved skills from shared skill libraries. We identify a vulnerability in this loop: during authoring, a retrieved malicious skill can become the template for a new skill that preserves the payload. We call this self-poisoning: the agent authors, stores, and runs the resulting malicious skill. We exploit it through EvoMal, an attack that amplifies self-poisoning by wrapping an interchangeable payload in a banner, a set of beni
top5.summary_zh: 此論文揭露自我演化 LLM 編碼代理的新型安全弱點:這類代理會把自寫工具存為「技能」,並從共享技能庫擷取相似技能當範本模仿改寫。攻擊者只需在庫中植入外觀正常的惡意技能,無須被代理呼叫;即使不含誘導橫幅,DeepSeek-V4-Pro 仍有 11.1% 的自我污染率,顯示弱點源自模仿式創作本身。EvoMal 以三層「橫幅」結構(逐字複製註解、裝飾器、匯入時註冊)包覆可替換的惡意酬載,誘使代理在改寫新技能時複製酬載並存回庫中,即「自我污染」;新副本再被後續任務擷取與再創作,形成自我傳播的蠕蟲。在 153 個 SWE-bench Verified 工具相關任務上,六種模型的代理自我污染率(ASPR)為 20.3% 至 41.8%,庫中惡意技能增至初始植入的 4.9 至 9.0 倍;僅改寫技能描述鎖定任務族群可將 ASPR 推升至 86.7%。移除植入技能後,Qwen3 第五輪仍達 68%,感染可自我維持。名稱封鎖、程式碼掃描與注入分類器皆難偵測代理自創的惡意技能;作者提出 counter-prompt 防禦,將 ASPR 壓至主要情境 ≤1.8%(個別情況 6.7%)且任務完成率無統計顯著下降,另建議簽章隔離閘門阻斷再擷取,並以分支過程 ρ=c·q·φ 說明傳播需兼具複製意願與技能可及性。限制:counter-prompt 屬軟性、依模型而異的緩解,分支模型預測與實測級聯仍有落差。此研究將安全邊界由攻擊者提交物轉向代理自創技能,對自演化代理的技能庫治理與供應鏈安全極具警示價值。

top5.title_zh: EvoMal:自我演化編碼代理中的自我污染攻擊

links.title: MemToC: Benchmarking Memory-Tool Conflict Resolution in Large Language Models

evidence: §1/§3.3: controlled post-tool-call setting with injected returns of known correctness enables four source-correctness cases plus tool-error and no-tool controls
§3.2: 3,912 sub-questions filtered to 605, then 575 with verified answers, blinded two-annotator QC yields 542 final questions; 542×4×3 = 6,504 episodes
§5.1 (Table 1): instruction-tuned baselines retain verified answers in only 6.5–17.1% of eligible cases vs 86.0–93.1% correct-tool following; incorrect-tool following 78.4–86.0%

§5.2: SFT and DPO meet the asymmetric criterion on the same two of four backbones (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, gemma-2-9b-it); Mistral SFT gains retention +41.8 but loses correct-tool following −27.6 and abstention −57.7
§5.4: prompting raises retention in 11/12 pooled combinations but every strategy reduces tool-error abstention for every model; abstain-and-flag cuts Llama correct-tool following 88%→24%
§5.4/App. G: tool-choice protocol is a model×protocol interaction; Llama drops 0.992→0.328 under free auto choice, repaired by schema-constrained decoding to 0.992, replicated at T=0.7
App. F.1: OOD transfer to FaithEval/ARC is positive but frame-dependent; abstention leak confirmed on all three transferred arms; disclosed matcher repair flipped one preregistered retention gate
§6: limitations—no proprietary models, single ToolHop core, 426/575 machine-authored distractors from one generator, annotators are authors, forced elicitation makes retention upper bounds
§8: benchmark, code, scoring layer, and per-claim map released Apache-2.0 with a verification script recomputing 180 reported values; two unrecomputable families are named rather than omitted
llm_evaluation.rationale: squarely in-scope LLM work: tool-augmented LLM arbitration between parametric memory and tool returns, evaluated on Llama/Qwen/Gemma/Mistral, mitigated with DPO/SFT and prompting. The controlled design—injecting tool returns of known correctness so arbitration (not mere source preference) is measurable (§1, §3.3)—is a genuine methodological advance over prior conflict benchmarks; the asymmetric success criterion and cross-fitted chain-level splits are thoughtful. Rigor is exceptional: preregistered protocol, Holm-corrected permutation tests with cluster bootstrap (§4.5, App. B), blinded scorer validation (κ=0.806, §4.2) and target validation (κ=0.785, §3.4), disclosed post-hoc matcher repair that flipped one gate (App. F.1), and honest negative results (prompting trade-offs §5.4, 19/20 arms reduce abstention; SAE steering asymmetry App. C). Evidence is strong with CIs, replication at T=0.7, and version provenance, though transfer rests on small verified pools (279/185 episodes) and two of four backbones lack seed replication. Generalizability is limited: only open-weight 7–9B models plus one confounded 70B probe (App. F.2), a single ToolHop-derived core with one distractor realization skewed to biographical domains, and annotators who are also authors (§6). Reproducibility is excellent: Apache-2.0 release with a verification script recomputing 180 values and a per-claim file map (§8), though fine-tuned absolute levels need unreleased training runs. Score reflects top-tier methodological care with moderate external validity.

primary_link.title: MemToC: Benchmarking Memory-Tool Conflict Resolution in Large Language Models

top5.summary: Tool-augmented LLMs must arbitrate between two fallible sources when a tool return conflicts with their parametric memory, yet existing evaluations measure source preference without establishing source correctness. We introduce MemToC, a controlled benchmark for post-tool-return arbitration with executable tools. MemToC comprises 6,504 evaluation episodes constructed from 542 quality-controlled factual questions, independently elicited model-specific closed-book answers, and controlled tool retu
top5.summary_zh: 工具增強的大型語言模型在工具回傳結果與其參數記憶矛盾時，必須在兩個都可能出錯的來源間仲裁，但既有評測往往只量測來源偏好，未事先確認來源正確性。本文提出 MemToC：自 ToolHop 資料集建構 542 道經品質控管的事實性問題，為每個模型獨立引出閉卷回答，再提供正確性已知的受控工具回傳，形成 6,504 個評測情境，依來源正確性劃分四種案例並設對照組，使仲裁行為而非單純偏好得以量測。在五個開放權重 7–9B 模型上，工具回傳強烈壓倒模型自身答案：四個指令微調模型在記憶正確而工具錯誤時，僅 6.5–17.1% 保留正確答案；工具正確時有 86.0–93.1% 跟隨；兩來源皆錯時仍有 78.4–86.0% 重複錯誤回傳，且排序在三種提示措辭間不穩定。作者以鏈層級交叉切分避免訓練與評測洩漏，比較提示策略與 SFT、DPO 微調，並採非對稱成功準則：正確答案保留率須提升，且正確工具跟隨率不得顯著下降。SFT 與 DPO 僅在相同兩個骨幹（Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct、gemma-2-9b-it）達標，顯示結果取決於骨幹多於最佳化目標；20 個方法—模型組合中有 19 個降低工具錯誤後的棄答率，增益常伴隨對工具的普遍不信任，外部遷移亦不完整且依模型而異。限制包括僅涵蓋 ToolHop 與開放權重模型、干擾答案建構單一、部分模型未做多種子驗證、強制引出使保留率成為上限，人工標記者亦為作者。本文將工具—記憶衝突重新框架為正確性條件化仲裁，凸顯評測須同時檢視正確工具使用、棄答與對措辭的穩健性。
top5.title: MemToC: Benchmarking Memory-Tool Conflict Resolution in Large Language Models
top5.title_zh: MemToC：評測大型語言模型的記憶—工具衝突解決能力

links.title: Candidate supply and answer selection shape the value of LLM judging in multi-agent systems

evidence: Abstract (p.1): combining answer frequency with judge evaluation 'raised accuracy from 63.82% to 70.82-70.95%' by rescuing outnumbered correct answers.
Results (p.4): open committee reached 42.20% accuracy at 10.73x token cost vs 41.06% for majority voting at 4.96x; oracle ceiling exceeded actual accuracy by 13.13-14.38 pp.

Results (p.6): judge rank AUC rises with availability, fitted half-rise midpoint pgen=14.7% (95% CI 14.3-15.1%, R2=0.900) over 15,336 questions, 67,163 pools, 823,988 pairs; fixed-composition 2C/6W control preserves the rise (m=12.2%, R2=0.887).
Results (pp.9-10): rationale-answer swap perturbation reduces rank AUC to 0.482 vs 0.684 unperturbed (+0.173, 95% CI 0.139-0.208) across 713 matched pools.

Results (p.12): first-ranked selection beats majority voting by +13.52 pp at k=2 but -0.34 pp (CI includes zero) at k=16; incremental judging cost escalates from US$0.10 to US$6.28 per 1,000 additional correct answers.

Methods/Software (pp.24-25): analysis code versioned at GitHub (release commit 7840cf3dbde77e61a1b4349ad3239669a7502431) and access-controlled Hugging Face archive with revision hash; seeds reported for all resampling procedures.

Extended Data Table 1 (pp.37-39): per-benchmark fit diagnostics; MuSR combinations frequently flagged low-R2/diagnostic, showing non-universal reliability boundaries across generators, judges, and tasks.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A general LLM-methods paper (not a domain application) squarely aligned with high-weight preferences: multi-agent LLM systems, LLM-as-judge evaluation, reasoning benchmarks, and test-time compute scaling. It decomposes multi-agent accuracy into candidate generation, judge recognition, and terminal selection, showing a 13-14 pp generation-retention gap (Methods, oracle upper bound, p.16) and that hybrid frequency+judge-rank selection lifts accuracy from 63.82% to 70.82-70.95% on 81,390 frozen pools (Abstract, p.1; Results, p.9). Rigor is exceptionally high: fixed-composition 2C/6W controls rule out displayed-ratio confounds (p.6), tie-breaking and odd/even pool-size sensitivities are run (p.12), rationale-answer swap perturbations isolate what the judge reads (+0.173 AUC, pp.9-10), bootstrap CIs with fixed seeds appear throughout, and low-R2 fits (e.g., MuSR) are honestly flagged in Extended Data Table 1. Novelty is moderate: it extends known results on self-consistency vs. debate and judge biases, but the availability-reliability sigmoid (half-rise 14.7%, R2=0.900, p.6) and the generation/selection attribution framework are fresh empirical contributions. Evidence is strong but tied to two closed preview APIs (DeepSeek-V4-Flash Preview, Mimo v2.5) and mostly multiple-choice verifiable tasks; open-ended and live-interaction settings are explicitly left open (Discussion, p.15). Reproducibility is strong: versioned GitHub code (commit 7840cf3) and a Hugging Face archive with revision hash (pp.24-25).
topics: reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, MuSR, MedXpertQA, HLE)

primary_link.title: Candidate supply and answer selection shape the value of LLM judging in multi-agent systems

top5.summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) sometimes already have the potential to answer correctly, but still report a wrong answer. Explaining this outcome is difficult because generation, communication and final answer-selection rules usually change simultaneously. We conceptualize multi-agent reasoning as an evolutionary pipeline of candidate generation, peer communication and terminal selection, wherein consensus without quality control can exhibit patterns of memetic drift. We study two questions: (1) when
top5.summary_zh: 多代理系統（MAS）有時明明已產生正確答案，最終卻回報錯誤結果。本文將多代理推理概念化為「候選生成、同儕溝通、終端選擇」三階段的演化式流程，指出在缺乏品質把關時，共識可能出現類似迷因漂移（memetic drift）與多數偏誤級聯的現象，使受歡迎的錯誤答案排擠少數正確答案。研究先以四種醫療推理協定檢視此瓶頸，再於 MMLU-Pro、GPQA、MedXpertQA、MuSR 共 15,336 題描繪 LLM 評審可信度（Humanity's Last Exam 另行分析），並以 16,278 題、81,390 個固定候選池進行離線重放實驗。三大發現：其一，正確答案常已存在於候選之中，系統卻仍輸出錯誤，形成 13.13–14.38 個百分點的「生成—保留缺口」；其二，評審可靠度並非模型的固定屬性，而隨任務、生成器與正確答案可用度（pgen）變化，低可用度時甚至低於隨機；其三，結合答案頻率與評審排序的混合選擇規則，將準確率由 63.82% 提升至 70.82–70.95%，主要來自拯救被多數錯誤淹沒的正確答案。成本分析顯示，評審在小候選池（k≤6）最具成本效益，池擴大後多數決優勢追平、評審效益遞減。限制在於離線重放隔離了動態互動中的接收者中介選擇與轉換過程。本研究為設計防止正確答案流失的多代理架構建立清晰的診斷基礎。
top5.title: Candidate supply and answer selection shape the value of LLM judging in multi-agent systems
top5.title_zh: 候選答案供給與答案選擇形塑 LLM 評審在多代理系統中的價值
